In this paper, electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were simultaneously recorded from 20 subjects undergoing emotion processing and regulation tasks.

description.value: Subjects observed neutral and negative visual stimuli and either passively watched them or regulated negative emotions by reappraisal.

stimuli.value: Standardized neutral and negative images obtained from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS)

description.value: Neutral visual-stimulus condition: participants viewed standardized neutral IAPS images after the watch cue and passively observed them.
Negative/unregulated visual-stimulus condition: participants viewed standardized negative IAPS images after the watch cue and passively observed them without regulating their emotions.

Negative emotion-regulation condition: participants viewed standardized negative IAPS images after the decrease cue and reappraised them by assigning a less unpleasant, more appealing, or neutral context.

instructions.value: When cued with “watch,” participants passively observed the following image. When cued with “decrease,” they regulated negative emotions by reinterpreting negative images in a less unpleasant manner, assigning them a more appealing or neutral context.

spans.text: When stimuli were preceded by the cue word “watch”, subjects were to passively observe the following image. When the cue word “decrease” was shown, subjects were to regulate their negative emotions by re-interpreting the negative images in a less unpleasant manner
